chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Safwan b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Abi al-Hazhaz from 'Ali b. al-Sirri. He said: I heard Aba 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying:

Surely, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) placed the sustenance of the believers in places they do not expect. And that is because when a servant does not know the source of his sustenance, he increases in his supplications.

key_terms.أَرْزَاقَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the sustenance of the believers -- Allah's provision specifically for the faithful
key_terms.كَثُرَ دُعَاؤُهُ: his supplication increases -- the spiritual fruit of material uncertainty
key_terms.مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا: from where they do not expect -- echoing Quran 65:3
key_terms.وَجْهَ رِزْقِهِ: the source/direction of his sustenance -- uncertainty about livelihood

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah place sustenance of believers where they do not expect according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this teaching from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), heard directly by 'Ali b. al-Sirri, the Imam explains a profound divine wisdom behind the uncertainty of livelihood. Allah deliberately places the sustenance of believers in unexpected sources — not to cause them hardship, but to draw them closer to Him through increased supplication (du'a). When a person cannot predict where their provision will come from, they naturally turn to Allah more frequently in prayer. This hadith echoes the Quranic verse 'And He provides for him from where he does not expect' (65:3) and reveals the spiritual benefit hidden within material uncertainty.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Safwan b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Abi’l Hajhaz from `Ali b. al-Sirri. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:
Surely, Allah put the sustenance of the believers in places that he does not expect. This is because, if a servant does not know where to find his sustenance, he increases in his supplications.
